Generate random Gaussian curves and pointwise summaries

Source: R/gaussian_curves_generator.R
gaussian_curves_generator.Rd

Generates standardized Gaussian white noise curves, smooths them, and returns the curves with their pointwise mean and sample standard deviation across curves. When only one curve is generated, the pointwise mean is that curve and the pointwise sample standard deviation is undefined, so sd contains NA values.

Usage

gaussian_curves_generator(sample_size, num_points, mu, sig, fwhm)

Arguments

sample_size

Positive integer giving the number of curves to generate.

num_points

Positive integer giving the number of evaluation points per curve.

mu

A finite number, or a numeric vector with one target mean per evaluation point. A scalar is used at every point and for every curve.

sig

A positive finite number, or a numeric vector with one target standard deviation per evaluation point. A scalar is used at every point and for every curve.

fwhm

Positive finite scalar giving the full width at half maximum used for smoothing.

Value

A list with three components: curves, a matrix with evaluation points in rows and curves in columns; sd, the pointwise sample standard deviation across curves; and mean, the pointwise mean across curves.

Examples

set.seed(123)
result <- gaussian_curves_generator(
  sample_size = 5, num_points = 100, mu = 0, sig = 1, fwhm = 4
)
dim(result$curves) # 100 5
#> [1] 100   5

# The target mean and SD can vary across evaluation points.
varied <- gaussian_curves_generator(
  sample_size = 3, num_points = 100,
  mu = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 100),
  sig = seq(0.5, 1.5, length.out = 100), fwhm = 4
)
dim(varied$curves) # 100 3
#> [1] 100   3

one_curve <- gaussian_curves_generator(
  sample_size = 1, num_points = 100, mu = 0, sig = 1, fwhm = 4
)
all(is.na(one_curve$sd)) # TRUE
#> [1] TRUE
identical(unname(one_curve$mean), unname(one_curve$curves[, 1])) # TRUE
#> [1] TRUE
